newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGB futures close lower but off earlier lows.
newsitem.headline: JGB futures close lower but off earlier lows.

text.p: The key March Japanese government bond (JGB) futures ended Thursday's Tokyo session down, but off earlier lows.
The March closed down 0.35 at 124.89. It opened at an intraday low of 124.64 following an overnight tumble in U.S. stock and bond prices.

Market sentiment was also dampened by a local financial daily report quoting a Bank of Japan (BOJ) official as saying the central bank may alter its monetary policy before assessing the possible economic impact of a planned hike in the consumption tax in April 1997, traders said.

According to Thursday's edition of the Nikkei Financial Daily, the BOJ official said: "The economy is stronger than we anticipated... It is possible that (the BOJ) may decide to alter monetary policy before examining the impact from a planned consumption tax increase."
After an initial sharp fall, the March contract had managed to erase some of its losses on bargain-hunting and short-covering, but met resistance at around 125.00.
"The market may be at a crucial point where people are searching for clues about the next move," said a trader at a city bank's securities unit.
In the cash market, investor bargain-hunting was seen in the benchmark when its yield moved above 2.5 percent, traders said.
The yield of the benchmark cash 182nd JGB stood at 2.480 percent as of 3.35 p.m. (0635 GMT), after rising as high as 2.530 percent in the morning. Wednesday's Tokyo close was 2.470 percent.
"Some investors were keen to buy cash JGBs at a yield of 2.5 percent or above," a brokerage house trader said.
Market participants would be watching U.S. financial markets for direction, traders said.
Players are concerned that a further weakness in U.S. stocks could push Tokyo's Nikkei 225 average below the key 20,000 level.
A Nikkei plunge below 20,000 may prompt some investors to take profits from their JGB holdings to cover losses, traders said.
The Nikkei ended Thursday's session down 67.18 points, or 0.33 percent, at 20,501.20, after falling as low as 20,321.32.
A 1.5 percent year-on-year fall in Japan's real household spending in October announced in the afternoon was virtually ignored by the JGB market, traders said.
"Household spending confirmed that consumption was weak, but the JGB market normally does not pay that much attention to this data," said a brokerage house trader.
After a 4.4 percent year-on-year decline in September, most economists had forecast real household spending would be flat in October, traders said.
